source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Aurora campus is the largest disclosed power block in Illinois at 114 MW of IT capacity, but most of the state's data centers disclose nothing at all.

The 114 MW is a published power envelope, not a machine count. Converting it to racks requires an assumed density that the operator does not supply. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training figure, the campus is roughly 2,850 racks. At 10 kW per rack it is about 11,400. The accelerator count depends on chips per rack, which is not published either. The power figure is the fact, and the rack and chip numbers are inferences from someone else's assumption.

Within Illinois, this campus ranks first by published megawatts among the six facilities that publish any figure. Those six total 236 MW, so Aurora is close to half of what the state has disclosed. The other 40 mapped facilities in Illinois publish no megawatt figure, which means the state's real capacity exceeds 236 MW and the ranking reflects disclosure rather than buildout. For AI scaling, the binding question is whether that 114 MW is delivered and energized, and the spec page does not say.

The data covers one campus's published specifications and the disclosure pattern across one state. It does not establish who occupies the space, what hardware runs there, or whether the capacity is live. The only certification listed is Green Globes, which speaks to environmental design and not to any tenant or workload. No address or postal code is published, so the physical siting within Aurora is not established here.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
